sections.content: Here's a question that stops most agents cold: "What are you actually making this month?" Not your projected GCI. Not your pipeline value. What will hit your bank account after splits, fees, taxes, and expenses?

If you don't know the answer, you're not alone. Most real estate agents track their income like they're driving with a fogged windshield—they can see shapes and movement, but they can't tell if they're about to hit something. You don't know what you're making this month because the numbers live in too many places: your brokerage statement, your spreadsheet, your gut feeling, and maybe a napkin calculation.
Why GCI Is a Dangerous Number to Track

Gross Commission Income feels good. It's big, it's exciting, and it's what agents brag about at networking events. But GCI is a vanity metric. It doesn't account for your split, transaction fees, marketing costs, or the months when deals fall through at the last second. Basing your financial decisions on GCI is like budgeting based on your lottery ticket expectations.
The True Cost of Income Uncertainty

When you don't know what you're actually making, you make poor decisions. You overspend during good months and panic during slow ones. You can't plan for taxes, can't budget for growth, and can't negotiate from a position of strength because you don't know what you actually need. This uncertainty creates stress that bleeds into every client interaction.

Know Your Numbers, Grow Your Business

Stop flying blind on your income. When you have clear visibility into what you're actually making—not just what you think you're making—you gain the confidence to make smart decisions, plan for growth, and build a business that lasts.
